policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere ואדעה and ketiv ואדע are both first-person singular 'that I may know', differing only in the cohortative he; ASV 'then tell me, that I may know' renders either identically. The verse's versional note ('So Septuagint, Vulgate, and Syriac. Hebrew he will.') is attached to the third-person verb behind 'if thou wilt not redeem it', not to this lemma, so it does not map here. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

ASV reads 'What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi', a second-person masculine singular verb addressed to the near kinsman, matching the qere קָנִיתָה. The ketiv קניתי is first-person singular ('I buy'), which the ASV wording excludes.

Qere לִגְאָל and ketiv לגאול differ only as defective and plene spellings of the same infinitive construct 'to redeem'; ASV 'I cannot redeem it' renders both alike and no note is mapped to this unit. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
